title: Traits and Adaptations
description: Traits are features of a living thing passed from parents to offspring. Adaptations are special traits that help an organism survive in its environment.

exercises.question: What is a TRAIT?
choices: a feature of a living thing passed from parent to offspring
exercises.exp: Traits are characteristics like eye colour, fur colour, or leaf shape that are inherited from parents.

exercises.question: A brown bear has brown fur. Its cub is also brown. Brown fur is a ___.
exercises.exp: Brown fur is inherited — the cub got this trait from its parents through genes.

exercises.question: What is an ADAPTATION?
choices: a special trait that helps an organism survive in its environment
the habitat where an animal lives
exercises.exp: Adaptations are inherited features that give an organism a survival advantage in its habitat.

exercises.question: A polar bear's WHITE fur helps it ___.
choices: camouflage in the snow to sneak up on prey
exercises.exp: White fur camouflages the polar bear in its snowy Arctic environment — a great adaptation for hunting!

exercises.question: A cactus has THICK stems and stores water. This adaptation helps it survive in ___.
exercises.exp: In the hot, dry desert, storing water in thick stems keeps a cactus alive when rain does not come for months.

exercises.question: Baby kittens look similar to their parents. This is because traits are ___.
exercises.exp: Genes carry information about traits from parents to offspring. Kittens inherit fur colour, ear shape, etc.

exercises.question: A duck has WEBBED FEET. This adaptation helps it ___.
choices: swim and paddle through water efficiently
exercises.exp: Webbed feet act like paddles — they push against water efficiently, helping ducks swim!

exercises.question: Which trait would be INHERITED (not learned)?
choices: knowing how to ride a bike
the shape of a person's nose
exercises.exp: Nose shape is determined by genes — you inherit it from your parents. Skills like biking are learned, not inherited.

exercises.question: A chameleon can change its COLOUR to match its surroundings. This is an adaptation for ___.
exercises.exp: Colour-changing camouflage helps chameleons hide from predators — an amazing survival adaptation!

exercises.question: Birds that eat fish often have LONG, SHARP BEAKS. This is an adaptation to ___.
choices: spear or grab fish from water
exercises.exp: Long, sharp beaks are perfect for catching slippery fish — the beak shape is adapted to the bird's diet.

exercises.question: Two dogs from the same litter look different. This shows that ___.
choices: traits are always identical between siblings
traits can vary even among related animals
exercises.exp: Siblings inherit a mix of genes from both parents, so traits vary — one pup might be spotted, another solid!

exercises.question: A porcupine's SHARP QUILLS are an adaptation to ___.
exercises.exp: Sharp quills stick into predators that attack, deterring them — perfect self-defence adaptation!

exercises.question: A GIRAFFE has a very long neck. This adaptation helps it ___.
choices: reach leaves high in trees that other animals cannot reach
exercises.exp: Giraffes' long necks let them eat from the tops of acacia trees where competition for food is lower — brilliant adaptation!

exercises.question: TWINS are born. One has brown eyes and one has blue eyes. What does this show?
choices: eye colour is random every time
traits can vary even between closely related individuals because genes mix differently
twins always have the same eye colour
eye colour is chosen by parents
exercises.exp: Even twins can have different traits if they receive different gene combinations from parents. Genetic variation is real!

exercises.question: A SNOW LEOPARD has thick spotted fur. Its spots help it ___.
choices: camouflage among rocky mountain terrain to sneak up on prey
exercises.exp: Snow leopard spots blend perfectly with rocky mountain landscapes — camouflage that helps them hunt and hide from threats.

exercises.question: Long EYELASHES on camels help them ___.
choices: block blowing sand in desert winds
exercises.exp: Camels have incredibly long eyelashes that act as shields against blowing desert sand — a brilliant desert adaptation!

exercises.question: Plants have ADAPTATIONS too. A THICK WAXY CUTICLE on desert plant leaves ___.
choices: reduces water loss from the leaf surface
exercises.exp: A waxy cuticle is waterproof — it seals the leaf surface to prevent precious water from evaporating in the hot desert.

exercises.question: What is the difference between INHERITED traits and LEARNED behaviours?
choices: they are exactly the same thing
inherited traits are passed through genes; learned behaviours are acquired through experience
learned behaviours are in genes; inherited traits are taught
there is no difference in animals
exercises.exp: Inherited traits (like fur colour) come from genes. Learned behaviours (like a dog sitting on command) come from experience and practice.

exercises.question: A WOODPECKER has a strong pointed beak. This is an adaptation to ___.
choices: chisel into wood to find insects and make nests
exercises.exp: A woodpecker's powerful, pointed beak is perfectly adapted for hammering into wood — up to 20 pecks per second!

exercises.question: ARCTIC FOXES have WHITE fur in winter and BROWN fur in summer. This helps them ___.
choices: camouflage in snow (white) in winter and in tundra vegetation (brown) in summer
exercises.exp: Arctic foxes change coat colour with the seasons — white in snow for winter camouflage, brown in summer tundra. Amazing adaptation!

exercises.question: A FISH'S STREAMLINED (smooth, tapered) body shape is an adaptation for ___.
choices: swimming efficiently by reducing water resistance
exercises.exp: Streamlined bodies reduce drag in water — fish slip through water smoothly because of their tapered shape.

exercises.question: TWINS raised apart in different families might have similar LOOKS but different SKILLS. This shows ___.
choices: genes have no effect on appearance
inherited traits (looks) are genetic, but many skills are learned from the environment
environment has no effect on people
exercises.exp: Genes determine physical traits (looks). Skills, languages, and habits are largely learned from environment and experience.

exercises.question: A HUMMINGBIRD has a LONG, THIN BEAK to ___.
choices: reach deep into tubular flowers to drink nectar
exercises.exp: Hummingbird beaks are perfectly shaped to fit inside tubular flowers — co-evolved with the flowers they pollinate!

exercises.question: Desert plants like CACTI store WATER in their thick stems. This is an adaptation to ___.
choices: survive months without rain in the desert
exercises.exp: Cacti store water in spongy tissue inside their stems — acting as a water reservoir during long dry periods in the desert.

exercises.question: A ZEBRA's stripes are an adaptation. Scientists think the stripes ___.
choices: help individual zebras find each other (each has a unique pattern) and may confuse predators and biting flies
make zebras visible to predators so they can run earlier
exercises.exp: Zebra stripes may help individuals recognise each other, confuse predators in a running herd, and deter biting flies!

exercises.question: A trait that helps an organism SURVIVE and REPRODUCE more successfully will ___.
choices: be passed to fewer offspring each generation
gradually become more common in the population over generations
exercises.exp: Helpful adaptations get passed on more — animals with the beneficial trait survive better and have more offspring. Over time, the trait spreads!

exercises.question: SUNFLOWERS track the SUN throughout the day (facing east in morning, west in evening). This is ___.
choices: a learned behaviour plants develop over time
an inherited plant adaptation called heliotropism that maximises sunlight for photosynthesis
exercises.exp: Heliotropism is a plant's ability to track the sun — young sunflowers do this to maximise sunlight absorption for photosynthesis!

exercises.question: A RHINOCEROS has thick skin. This adaptation ___.
choices: protects it from scratches, insect bites, and minor injuries
exercises.exp: Rhinos' thick, tough skin is like armour — protecting them from thorny bushes, insect bites, and the sun's heat.

exercises.question: Scientists observe that FAST CHEETAHS catch more prey than slow ones. What will likely happen over many generations?
choices: speed has no effect on cheetah populations
faster cheetahs will survive and reproduce more — the cheetah population will tend toward greater speed over time
all cheetahs will become the same speed
exercises.exp: Natural selection: faster cheetahs catch more food, survive better, and have more offspring. Speed is favoured and spreads through the population!

exercises.question: Which of these is a BEHAVIOURAL adaptation (not a physical one)?
choices: bears hibernating in winter to survive food shortage
exercises.exp: Hibernation is a behavioural adaptation — bears do not physically change, but their BEHAVIOUR (sleeping all winter) helps them survive.

exercises.question: WEBBED FEET in ducks, FLIPPERS in seals, and FINS in fish all serve the same purpose. What is it?
choices: swimming and moving efficiently through water
exercises.exp: Different animals evolved different structures (webbed feet, flippers, fins) to solve the same problem — moving through water!

exercises.question: A trait that is INHERITED is one that is ___.
choices: passed from parent to offspring through genes
exercises.exp: Inherited traits come from parents through DNA/genes — like eye colour, fur colour, or blood type. You are born with them!

exercises.question: Which of these is an INHERITED trait in humans?
choices: being able to ride a bicycle
blood type (A, B, AB, or O)
exercises.exp: Blood type is determined by genes from your parents — you are born with it. Riding a bike and language are learned traits.

exercises.question: A LEARNED behaviour is one that ___.
choices: is acquired through experience and observation
is shared by all members of a species
exercises.exp: Learned behaviours develop through experience — like a dog learning tricks, or a human learning to cook. Not inherited!

exercises.question: Lion cubs learn to hunt by watching and practising. This is a ___.
choices: inherited trait — cubs are born knowing how to hunt
learned behaviour — they develop hunting skills through experience and play
exercises.exp: While instinct drives the DESIRE to hunt, the specific skills — stalking, pouncing, working in groups — are learned through practice and observation.

exercises.question: A baby bird INSTINCTIVELY opens its mouth when the nest shakes. This is ___.
choices: a learned behaviour — the bird practised this
an instinct — an inborn behaviour the bird did not need to learn
an adaptation that happened in the bird's lifetime
exercises.exp: Instincts are inborn — baby birds do not learn to beg; they do it automatically. Opening mouths when the nest shakes signals hunger!

exercises.question: IDENTICAL TWINS have the same genes but may look slightly different if they have different life experiences. This shows ___.
choices: genes have no effect on appearance
both genes AND environment (diet, exercise, sun exposure) affect traits
environment has no effect on traits
exercises.exp: Even identical twins with the same DNA can differ — different diets, exercise, and environments affect how genes are expressed!

exercises.question: Which of these shows VARIATION in a population?
choices: cats in the same litter can be different colours and sizes
exercises.exp: Variation means differences within a species — different colours, sizes, and patterns in a litter show genetic variation!

exercises.question: Natural selection favours traits that ___.
choices: help organisms survive and reproduce in their environment
exercises.exp: Natural selection: traits that improve survival/reproduction are passed to offspring more often — the population gradually changes.

exercises.question: A GIRAFFE'S long neck helps it reach leaves high in trees. This is an example of ___.
choices: an adaptation (inherited physical trait that improves survival)
a sign the giraffe is sick
a random characteristic with no purpose
exercises.exp: A long neck is a physical adaptation — giraffes with longer necks reach more food, survive better, and have more offspring!

exercises.question: An animal's COAT COLOUR can be an inherited trait. If light-coloured moths are harder for birds to spot on pale trees, over time the moth population will have ___.
choices: more light moths — they are better camouflaged and survive more
no moths — they all get eaten
exercises.exp: Light moths survive predation better → they reproduce more → light colour becomes more common in the population. Natural selection!

exercises.question: Why do offspring resemble their parents but are NOT identical?
choices: they copy their parent's appearance exactly
offspring inherit a mix of genes from both parents, plus mutations can occur
parents always look different from their children
genes are chosen randomly with no inheritance
exercises.exp: Offspring get half their genes from each parent — giving a unique mix. This is why you may have mum's eyes and dad's hair!

exercises.question: Which statement about INSTINCT is TRUE?
choices: instincts must be learned from parents
instincts are inherited behaviours an animal is born with
instincts change throughout an animal's life
exercises.exp: Instincts are inborn — baby spiders spin webs, salmon swim upstream, and sea turtles head to the ocean without being taught!

exercises.question: Why do MUTATIONS in genes sometimes help a species survive?
choices: a mutation might create a new useful trait that improves survival in a changing environment
mutations have no effect at all
exercises.exp: Most mutations are neutral or harmful, but occasionally one creates a useful new trait — like antibiotic-resistant bacteria. Evolution in action!

exercises.question: A farmer selectively breeds cows that produce the MOST milk. Over generations, the herd produces more milk. This is called ___.
exercises.exp: Artificial selection (selective breeding) is when humans choose which animals breed — selecting for desired traits like milk production.

exercises.question: Humans and chimpanzees share about 98% of their DNA. This suggests ___.
choices: they share a common ancestor and are closely related
they are exactly the same species
exercises.exp: Shared DNA is evidence of a common ancestor. The more similar the DNA, the more closely related two species are — 98% is very close!

exercises.question: A kitten raised by dogs might act more 'dog-like' in some ways. This is an example of ___.
choices: a learned behaviour shaped by its environment
exercises.exp: Some behaviours are influenced by environment and upbringing. The kitten learns dog-like behaviours — but its DNA is still cat DNA!

exercises.question: Fossils show that many animals that existed millions of years ago are now EXTINCT. What does this tell us?
choices: species change over time and those that cannot adapt to environmental changes may die out
life on Earth has never changed
exercises.exp: The fossil record shows species appear, change, and go extinct. Species that cannot adapt to environmental changes disappear forever.

exercises.question: What is CAMOUFLAGE an example of?
choices: a physical adaptation that helps an organism blend into its environment
a type of mimicry (acting like something else)
exercises.exp: Camouflage is a physical adaptation — body patterns and colours that match the environment make the animal harder to spot by predators or prey.

exercises.question: A dog can be taught to sit, shake, and fetch. These are all examples of ___.
choices: learned behaviours developed through training and reward
instincts the dog was born with
exercises.exp: Sitting, shaking, and fetching are all trained (learned) behaviours — the dog associates actions with rewards through repeated practice.

exercises.question: Which of these is an INSTINCT in newborn humans?
choices: the sucking reflex — newborns automatically suck when something touches their lips
exercises.exp: The sucking reflex is an instinct — newborns automatically know how to suck for feeding. Walking and talking are learned over months/years!
